pair_convention.spot_explanation: GBP/CHF at 1.10417 means 1 GBP = 1.10417 CHF (30 October 2026 close). Rising = GBP strengthening vs CHF; falling = GBP weakening vs CHF. This is a cross with no dollar leg. It pairs a high-yielding currency from an energy-importing economy with a current account deficit against Europe's classic safe haven, which pays no interest and runs a large external surplus.

executive_summary: GBP/CHF closed at 1.10417 on 30 October 2026. The pair is quoted in francs per pound, so a rising pair means a stronger pound. It is up 0.69% over one month, 1.45% over three months, 4.37% over six months and 5.42% over a year, and sits at the 94th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 1.03555-1.10859. The dominant story is carry against the haven. Bank Rate at 3.75% against the SNB's 0% is a 375bp gap, rising to 400bp if the Bank of England hikes on 5 November. No SNB meeting falls before 10 December, and the listed futures spread prices about 449bp a year of forward discount. Against that sit two live haven tails: a post-midterm US-Iran escalation window and French sovereign stress. The bilateral reading is sharper than either currency view on its own. Both currency views are Neutral tactically, but against each other the BoE-SNB divergence reinforces in the pound's favour over four weeks. Over six months the bearish pound view (UK deficit of 2.5% of GDP, a BoE delivering less than priced) and the mildly bullish franc view (surplus of 9.2% of GDP, a 2027 SNB hike option) point the same way. Tactical stance: Bullish, conviction 2, weighted score +0.12, base case 1.1110 by 27 November. Strategic stance: Bearish, conviction 2, weighted score -0.28, base case 1.0760 by 30 April 2027. There are two caveats. The tactical upside has to clear a ten-touch resistance band at 1.10955-1.11969, starting 54 pips above spot, from inside a coiling symmetrical triangle. The six-month forward at about 1.0794 already discounts a 248-pip decline, so the strategic call is a spot-direction call that a forward short barely monetises. A numeric UBS path, 1.12 in December 2026, declining to 1.09 by March 2027 and 1.08 by June and September 2027, has the same up-then-down shape as both horizons here.

market_context.valuation_assessment: The cross is near the top of its 52-week range but far below long-run purchasing-power parity. World Bank PPP (GBP and CHF dossiers) puts GBP/CHF fair value at 1.3745, so the pound is 19.7% cheap against the franc, or equivalently the franc carries a 24.5% premium. UBS puts long-term equilibrium at 1.13, a more relevant multi-year anchor and still 258 pips above spot. Real effective rates diverge: the BIS real broad index for the franc fell to 98.37 in September, the lowest of 33 monthly readings since January 2024, while sterling's is 111.48, about its 55th percentile. What is priced is a carry premium that has eroded part of the franc's long-run PPP premium. A gap of 20% or more against PPP has no record of closing inside six months, so valuation sets no cap or floor on either horizon. A franc at a 33-month real low is no longer expensive enough to squeeze the Swiss surplus, which is scored under Factor 5.

market_context.recent_regime: From May to September the pair traded as a franc-funded carry trade. It rose from about 1.0480 to a 30 September closing high of 1.10859 as the BoE turned hawkish and the SNB held at zero. The one break came on 1 October. Haven demand tied to French spread stress and the Gulf took the pair from a 1.11079 intraday high to a 1.09662 close (-1.08% in a session), and to 1.08885 intraday the next day. That single day erased about three months of futures-implied carry. Since then, carry has reasserted itself inside a narrowing triangle, while the haven bid proved intermittent. Rabobank argued that pound-franc fell from near 1.11 to 1.09 in the first week of October, and has since recovered most of that drop. The last six closes sat in a 12-pip band at 1.1034-1.1046, a market waiting for the Bank of England.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Policy carry is 375bp a year (Bank Rate 3.75% against the SNB at 0%), rising to 400bp after a 25bp BoE hike on 5 November. Futures-implied carry is about 449bp a year (annualised December 2026 to March 2027 CME franc and sterling futures calendar spread, observed 29 October), about 74bp beyond the policy gap, consistent with the November hike and part of a further BoE move being priced while the SNB is priced near zero; it combines the rate differential with any cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated without an OIS curve. The annualised_carry_bps field uses the 375bp policy carry; on the 449bp futures-implied rate the figure is 448.7bp. Carry-to-vol is 0.69 on policy carry over the 5.437% estimated three-month implied vol (0.83 on futures carry); on 60-day realised vol (5.17%) it is 0.73 and 0.87; on a likely true implied vol of about 6.2% it is 0.60 and 0.72. On any measure it is the best carry-to-vol among pound crosses. Carry regime is working: over six months spot rose 4.37% and the position accrued about 1.9% of carry, for a total return of roughly 6.3%. The fragility is conditional, not structural: the 1 October session showed how a haven bid can give back months of accrual in a day.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: High-carry pair: the 375bp policy gap, widening to 400bp after a Bank of England hike, is the widest positive differential the pound holds against any G10 currency. The futures-implied carry is about 449bp a year. Boosted by 0.03 on both horizons.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Bank Rate is 3.75% and the SNB policy rate is 0%, a 375bp differential. It widens to 400bp if the Bank of England hikes on 5 November, which is about 95% priced and which ING calls a done deal. The SNB's next assessment is 10 December, after the four-week window. So for the whole tactical horizon the differential can only stay where it is or widen from the UK side. The listed futures calendar spread for the cross, observed 29 October, prices a GBP/CHF forward discount of about 449bp a year. That is roughly 74bp more than today's policy gap, consistent with the November hike and part of a further BoE move being priced, while the SNB is priced near zero: about 6bp for December in mid-October, down from roughly even odds in late September. The pair transmits this mainly through carry. On an estimated three-month implied volatility of 5.4%, carry-to-vol is near 0.7, the best of any pound cross. That keeps franc-funded positions in place while volatility stays low. The risk on 5 November is a 'dovish hike', with Chief Economist Pill sceptical of the four hikes priced. That would trim pricing of later BoE moves, not the 400bp gap that starts accruing straight away. This is where the two currency views reinforce each other: the pound's policy factor is Neutral on its own, but the franc's is Bearish because every peer is tightening while the SNB holds.

The edge is carry building up over a window with no SNB meeting. A dovish Monetary Policy Report that trims 2027 BoE pricing is the downside surprise, and it matters less for this cross than for GBP/USD because the SNB is not tightening either.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the question moves from the level of the differential to the surprise against what is priced, and on that both currency views point against the pair. The curve prices Bank Rate near 4.75% within a year. The base view expects a 4.25% terminal, citing Pill's scepticism, the OBR's assumption of just over 4.25% by mid-2027 and a group of banks forecasting two hikes; UBS expects the November move plus one more in the first quarter of 2027. In Switzerland the 2-year yield fell from 0.263% to 0.18% during October as hike pricing faded. Yet the franc view puts the chance of an SNB hike by March 2027 at about 30%, more than the curve implies. If both are right, the differential settles near 400-425bp rather than the 450bp-plus the futures imply, a negative surprise of 25-50bp. Even the dovish path still leaves the pound's widest carry and a 10-year yield gap of 482bp on 30 October closes (5.29% against 0.47%), so the absolute cushion remains. The level supports the pair and the expected repricing works against it, which nets to Neutral. The dated tests are the SNB assessment and new conditional forecast on 10 December, the BoE decision on 17 December (no Report), and the Monetary Policy Report on 4 February 2027, a provisional date.

On that figure carry-to-vol is about 0.83 and breakevens are about 41, 124 and 248 pips. The regime works in calm markets and breaks in haven episodes; that fragility is scored under Factors 3 and 7.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation gap is 250bp on headline (UK 3.5% against Swiss 1.0% in September) and 230bp on core (2.8% against 0.5%). Its direction is what keeps the two central banks apart. UK services inflation rose to 3.7%, the October flash composite PMI reached an eight-month high of 53.1, and unemployment fell to 4.7%. In Switzerland core is still 0.5%, nominal wages are rising only 0.4% in 2026, and the KOF barometer slipped to 107.6 from 109.1. UK data have been surprising hawkishly, while Swiss data have been broadly in line. The UK calendar inside four weeks is dense: Q3 GDP on 12 November, labour data on 17 November and October CPI in the third week of November. The base view expects those to beat the Bank's own assumptions. The one Swiss release that matters, October CPI on 3 November, is close to a coin flip around 1.0%. The pair is therefore more sensitive to UK data: UK releases can lift the 2027 BoE strip, while the Swiss print would need to reach 1.2% or more to revive a December SNB hike. The one discordant UK signal, GfK confidence at -24, matters more over months than over weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months the growth-inflation mix turns against the pound relative to the franc. The UK is heading into an energy-driven stagflation. The Bank projects CPI slightly above 4% in Q1 2027, the OBR has cut 2027 growth to 1.0%, and GfK confidence fell 11 points to -24. Inflation stays high for reasons that erode real incomes rather than justify a longer hiking cycle. Switzerland is at the other end. Inflation is rising from the lowest base in G10: the SNB's conditional path is 0.7% for 2026 and 0.8% for 2027 at a 0% rate. SECO forecasts growth of 1.7% in 2026 and 1.6% in 2027, and energy carries roughly half the euro area's weight in the Swiss CPI basket. So UK growth slows towards 1% with high inflation, while Swiss growth stays near trend and inflation edges towards the level that opens a hike option. The effect on the pair comes through policy surprise: stagflation lets the BoE stop early and firmer Swiss inflation lets the SNB move off zero, and both narrow the differential relative to pricing. Confidence is modest because pharmaceuticals flattered Swiss growth and both the KOF and the PMI are turning lower.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: GBP/CHF pairs the high-yielding currency of an energy importer with Europe's haven, so its beta to risk aversion is moderate and negative: in stress the franc gains and the pound, a carry destination rather than a funder, loses. The broad backdrop is middling rather than risk-off, with the VIX at 17.2 and US equities near records, but two specific stresses are live. The first is European sovereign stress. The OAT-Bund spread reached 152.5bp, the widest since 2011, and the franc gained more than 2% against the euro in October. That reaches this cross whenever the franc's gains against the euro outpace the pound's. The second is the window after the US midterms in which the White House has said strikes on Iran become possible. The base view puts a four-week escalation at 30%, against 10% for a Hormuz framework. Escalation hits the pair through both legs at once: higher UK gas costs and a haven bid for the franc. US high-yield spreads near the wide end of their one-year range add to the downside tail. Rabobank notes that the franc's haven bid has been intermittent this month and has not stopped the carry, which keeps confidence low.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months both risk tails are live and roughly balanced for this pair. A winter Gulf escalation or a disorderly euro-area sovereign episode would compound against GBP/CHF: the pound suffers as an energy importer with a deficit, and the franc gains as the haven. A US-Iran settlement that reopens Hormuz, or a French political resolution, would do the reverse just as strongly: UK gas would fall and the franc's haven premium would drain back into carry. The base view puts escalation and settlement at about 15% each over six months. The franc view sees the distribution as wide but centred, with strong equities, a 7% fall in gold in October and the carry incentive offsetting the French stress. Credit at the wide end of its range against equities near records is a late-cycle divergence that usually resolves towards wider spreads, a mild risk to the pair. But the pound's beta to broad risk is moderate, and it is a funding-currency unwind, not a spread move, that would hurt the pair most. With the tails symmetric in probability and in their effect on the pair, the factor carries no edge.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two legs are crowded in opposite directions by different investors. In sterling, the legacy non-commercial net short of 79,400 contracts sits on the 80,000 line that has marked stretched pound shorts. Asset managers are short 128,893 contracts, largely structural hedging, and UBS and ING both flag the large sterling short as fuel for covering if the BoE sounds hawkish. In francs, leveraged funds are net short 17,502 contracts, the most in 25 weeks, while asset managers are the least short of the window. Read across the pair, fast money is effectively long GBP/CHF: leveraged funds hold a sterling long of 17,195 contracts and their largest franc short since May, which is the carry trade itself. Real money is short the pound and covering franc shorts. A hawkish BoE on 5 November would squeeze the sterling short in the pair's favour; a haven shock would squeeze the leveraged franc short against it. Option skew on both dollar legs (GBP/USD one-month risk reversal -0.53 vols, USD/CHF -0.80 vols) implies a cross skew towards GBP/CHF downside. Leveraged funds also cut their sterling long by 6,909 contracts in the latest week. These forces offset.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months positioning describes who holds the risk rather than signalling direction. Asset managers' sterling short has stayed between -89,211 and -156,307 contracts all year. It reflects UK pension and insurer hedging of foreign assets and changes only if hedge ratios do, which would need a sustained rise in UK real yields relative to the rest of the world. Swiss institutions' structural franc shorts, also hedges, have been cut 42% from their July peak. That leaves less real-money franc selling to come, and they could rebuild if European stress fades. Leveraged funds' long-GBP, short-CHF carry has built steadily as differentials widened and can keep growing while the BoE hikes and volatility stays low. Six-month skews (GBP/USD -0.90 vols, USD/CHF -0.68 vols) show longer-dated hedgers paying for pound downside and franc upside, a mild bearish signal for the cross. But neither leg is at a forced-liquidation extreme: the franc short is below the roughly 30,000 contracts that preceded past squeezes. No positioning extreme forces a six-month move, so the factor is Neutral.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Leveraged funds hold the pair's carry trade (long GBP, short CHF, the franc short at its 25-week maximum), while real money is structurally short sterling. Speculative crowding sits on the long side of the cross; hedging crowding sits on the short side of the pound.
tactical.unwind_trigger: A haven shock unwinds the leveraged long: a post-midterm US strike on Iran, an OAT-Bund spread above 170bp, or a VIX close above 25. A 9-0 BoE hike with guidance for more on 5 November would instead squeeze the legacy sterling short.
tactical.historical_analogue: At the outbreak of the US-Iran war in early March 2026, demand for francs was strong enough that the SNB intervened to slow it. That is the template for how fast a haven rush can overwhelm franc-funded carry.
tactical.contrarian_case: The consensus trade is long GBP/CHF for carry: UBS calls it one of the more attractive G10 total-return trades, and fast money has built the largest franc short since May. Being crowded into a carry trade funded in the haven currency, ahead of a dated geopolitical window, is exactly the setup in which carry gives back months of accrual in days. The contrarian case is that the risk is to the downside and arrives suddenly, while the upside from sterling short-covering is already partly spent.

strategic.unwind_trigger: A change in UK hedge ratios after a sustained rise in UK real yields, which is not our base case, would cover sterling shorts. Swiss institutions rebuilding franc hedges as French stress fades would add franc selling. Both lift the pair.
strategic.historical_analogue: The 2023 reversal in UK institutional hedging flows produced a large and persistent sterling move once hedge ratios changed. The base view puts a repeat inside six months below 15%.
strategic.contrarian_case: Long-dated skew on both legs pays for a weaker pound and a stronger franc, and the structural views (a UK deficit and a Swiss surplus) agree. The contrarian risk runs the other way: if European stress fades, Swiss asset managers could rebuild about 18,000 contracts of franc hedges towards their July level. That would be franc selling that strategic models do not anticipate.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external gap is among the widest in G10. The UK ran a current account deficit of 2.5% of GDP in Q2 2026, while Switzerland ran a surplus of 9.2% (OECD) on a CHF 23.7bn quarterly surplus, a difference of about 11.7 percentage points. In bilateral goods trade, UK-reported figures show the UK exported $9.3bn to Switzerland in 2024 and imported $12.8bn, a $3.5bn deficit against Switzerland. Swiss-reported exports to the UK of $22.6bn are far larger. The gap is most plausibly gold and precious-metals routing, so we use the UK-reported net figure. Terms of trade are moving against the pound at the margin. The Q1 2027 UK gas contract made a record close on 28 October and was about 238p/therm on 30 October, and Brent physical assessments were $123.10. Energy is only about 3.5% of the Swiss CPI basket, so the franc's import bill barely moves. Under the commodity rules, oil and gas up are pound-negative, and the only franc commodity link, gold, fell 7% in October, which slightly offsets. strategic.bilateral_analysis: At the strategic weight this is the clearest structural force on the pair, and the two currency views agree on it. The UK must finance a 2.5%-of-GDP deficit every quarter. Its primary income account is worsening as foreigners earn more on gilts, and Q1 2027 gas forwards are more than double the Q2 2026 average of about 112p/therm. The base view expects the deficit to widen back above 3% of GDP in the Q4 and Q1 data. Switzerland's surplus is large and persistent: the IMF projects 6.2% of GDP for 2026, and net foreign assets near CHF 1tn generate steady income. The BIS real effective rate for the franc is at 98.37, its lowest since at least January 2024, against 111.48 for sterling at about its 55th percentile. That means the franc is no longer expensive enough in real terms to squeeze the surplus, while the pound is not cheap enough to correct the deficit through competitiveness. The US pharmaceutical tariff on Switzerland is settled at 15%, which reduces the risk of another export collapse. A debtor energy importer facing a record winter gas forward, against a creditor with a modest energy bill, needs either a weaker exchange rate or higher real yields, and the base view expects the BoE to supply less of the second than priced.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The UK is a net energy importer. Under the direction rules oil up is pound-negative (-GBP) and natural gas (TTF and the UK NBP) up is pound-negative (-GBP). The base view treats UK gas as the decisive input through the Ofgem cap and the winter import bill.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland imports energy but with a small weight (about 3.5% of CPI), and the direction rules give the franc no oil or gas sensitivity. Gold up is franc-positive (+CHF) through the haven correlation.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Step 1, oil: oil up gives -GBP, while CHF has no listed oil exposure and a low energy weight (about 0). Net: the pair falls. Step 2, gas: TTF/NBP up gives -GBP, with no listed CHF exposure. Net: the pair falls. Step 3, gold: gold up gives +CHF, GBP unaffected. Net: the pair falls. Step 4, correlation: in Gulf escalations energy and gold usually rise together and the franc also draws a haven bid, so the channels compound rather than offset. October's mix of higher energy and a 7% fall in gold was a partial exception that softened the franc's support. Net: energy and gold strength are consistently negative for GBP/CHF, and commodity weakness is consistently positive.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Pair falls. The pound absorbs a larger import bill and a higher Q1 2027 CPI peak, while the franc is barely affected and, if the rise comes from Gulf escalation, gains a haven bid.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair rises. UK terms of trade improve and the BoE's stagflation dilemma eases, while a de-escalation-driven fall in oil drains the franc's haven premium back into carry.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: UK wholesale gas (the NBP Q1 2027 forward), which sets the winter import bill and the January Ofgem cap. Gold is the secondary channel through the franc.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Only one central-bank communication falls inside four weeks: the BoE's 5 November decision with its Monetary Policy Report. The SNB is silent until its 10 December assessment. The BoE's message pulls two ways. Governor Bailey warned on 9 October that looking through energy works only if expectations stay anchored, which markets read as tolerance running out. But Pill, one of the three hawks, has said a hike should not signal a series and that he is sceptical of four hikes priced. The base view expects a 7-2 or 8-1 hike with projections that push back on the 2027 strip, a dovish hike, against a smaller chance of a 9-0 vote that endorses more. On the Swiss side, the 22 October summary of deliberations dropped the 'increased willingness' to intervene. That removes a cap on franc strength, but it matters mostly near the euro levels the SNB defends and is not a near-term force on this cross. Both banks are credible, and the guidance differential is unchanged on the day: hawkish action from the BoE, a hold from the SNB, and cautious BoE wording that offsets the action.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months guidance points to a narrower policy gap than priced, from both ends. The BoE's projections are conditioned on a curve pricing about 100bp, so if successive Reports show inflation at or below target at the policy horizon, the Committee is signalling that the market has gone too far. The 4 February 2027 Report, a provisional date, is the base view's inflection point. A credible bank that says it does not need four hikes will be believed, and that works against the pound here. The SNB's guidance is drifting slightly hawkish. Its September conditional forecast already showed medium-term inflation edging higher, partly because of the weaker franc. The December assessment brings a new forecast that the franc view expects to raise 2027 inflation to 0.9-1.0%. The board has also stepped back from leaning against franc strength. The SNB has a record of surprising markets, and with the rate at zero and inflation rising, its surprise risk now points hawkish. A BoE pushing back on its curve and an SNB edging away from permanent zero both narrow the expected differential, which is Bearish for the pair.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The UK's main domestic tail, the 28 October Budget, is out of the way: it kept £14.5bn of headroom and gilts held steady. Swiss domestic politics are quiet, and the 29 November federal votes are not macro events. The dated binary risks are external, and their effect on the pair is skewed one way. After the 3 November US midterms a strike on Iran becomes possible. The base view puts escalation within four weeks at 30% and a Hormuz framework at 10%, and escalation hits this cross through both legs: the pound as an energy importer and the franc as a haven. The French political and fiscal crisis is the second live risk. The franc view puts a French government collapse at about 15% within four weeks; it would draw haven flows into the franc and only partly into sterling. Event clustering matters: Swiss CPI and the midterms on 3 November and the BoE on 5 November fall in the same week. A hawkish BoE could be swamped by an escalation within days. The upside events for the pair (a 9-0 BoE vote, a Hormuz deal) are less likely than the downside ones.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months event risk is asymmetric between the two economies. The UK faces dated fiscal and political tests: the spring fiscal statement and 2027 Spending Review, welfare decisions pushed into 2027, pressure to unfreeze the personal allowance, and an electricity VAT cut that expires in March unless extended, all under a new government with thin headroom. Switzerland's political calendar is routine. Its EU treaty package is advancing after a 29-15 Council of States vote, and US tariffs are settled at 15%. The shared geopolitical tail is the Iran war. A winter escalation would compound against the pair through UK energy costs and the franc's haven bid, and a settlement would do the reverse. The base view nets the large-move scenarios slightly against the pound, with a disorderly gilt sell-off on a fiscal U-turn at about 10%, Brent above $140 at 15% and a Hormuz settlement at 15%. The franc side carries an offsetting risk that the SNB returns to active intervention if franc strength gets disorderly, which caps rather than reverses the downside. The balance tilts Bearish at modest confidence.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The fiscal gap is wide and stable. UK government debt is about 103% of GDP and rising towards 107% on Moody's projections, with ratings of AA, Aa3 and AA-. Switzerland's gross debt is about 38% of GDP, it is rated AAA and Aaa, and its debt brake produced a 2025 federal surplus. In October the gap between the two was live through gilts: the 30-year touched 6.07% and the 10-year 5.44%, while Swiss 10-year yields fell 11bp on haven demand. The Budget then cleared the market test. Healey kept £14.5bn of headroom and moved issuance away from the long end, and 10-year gilts eased to 5.29%. Borrowing is still running £6.0bn above the OBR's path for the first half of the fiscal year, so the margin is thin. But there is no UK fiscal event inside four weeks, and Swiss fiscal quality is fully priced in yields 482bp below gilts. With no catalyst to reprice either side over the tactical window, the differential is real but inactive, so the factor is Neutral.

UK headroom of £14.5bn is small next to forecast errors already accumulating. Borrowing is £6.0bn above plan after six months, and the OBR gives only a 56% chance of meeting the rules, while debt service rises with gilt yields near 5.3% at ten years. Spending pressure is building, and the rating agencies last acted before the 2026 energy shock, so an outlook change in 2027 is a live sterling risk. Switzerland's challenges are small by comparison: structural federal deficits of CHF 2-4bn a year before relief measures, and defence and pension costs within a debt brake, against fiscal space that lets it absorb a downturn without market strain. The contrast matters for the pair because the franc collects haven allocations whenever European sovereign quality is questioned. A renewed UK gilt premium, which the base view expects at 20-30bp at the long end in the spring, would hit the pound directly. The dated UK tests are the spring fiscal statement and the 2027 Spending Review.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: GBP/CHF has no listed option anywhere, so its implied volatility can only be estimated from the two dollar legs. That estimate, observed 29 October, is 5.15% at about one month, 5.44% at three months and 5.79% at six months, a contango term structure. It is built with realised rather than implied correlation and has historically run low, so the true level is probably closer to 6%. Either way, this is a low-volatility cross, which is what makes the 375bp carry so attractive on a carry-to-vol basis. The leg skews carry the directional information. GBP/USD one-month risk reversals at -0.53 vols pay for pound downside and USD/CHF at -0.80 vols pay for franc upside, so both legs imply a cross skew towards GBP/CHF falling. The leg vols carry a modest event premium for 3-5 November (GBP/USD implied 0.94 vols over realised, USD/CHF 0.98), and there is no backwardation into a single date. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Dollar liquidity is ample and orderly. SOFR was 3.94% inside a 3.75-4.00% target range after the Fed's 10-2 hold on 28 October with two dissents for a hike. Reserve balances are near $2.96tn, Fed assets are broadly flat at $6,753.6bn, and central-bank swap-line use is negligible at $170m, so neither the BoE nor the SNB is drawing dollars. For a cross this matters through two opposing channels. Calm funding keeps franc-funded carry comfortable, which supports the pair, and the franc view scores it franc-negative for that reason. But year-end dollar demand from late November falls on UK banks, which are large dollar borrowers through London, and a December Fed hike strengthens the dollar against both legs about equally. Neither GBP nor CHF cross-currency basis is published by a free source, and the leg futures rolls show no dollar premium on either side. The dollar effects largely cancel inside the cross. The carry-supporting effect of calm funding is already scored under Factors 1 and 3, so to avoid counting it twice this factor is Neutral.

The relevant channel for this cross is the dollar smile. On the right side, with the Fed hiking and US exceptionalism, the dollar gains broadly and franc-funded carry into sterling keeps working. On the left side, in global risk-off, the dollar and the franc gain together while the pound, a carry destination, underperforms, so the pair falls. If the Fed's hiking phase ends in the first half of 2027, as the franc view expects, the dollar drifts to the middle of the smile, where cross effects are muted. Swiss institutions are structural dollar borrowers for foreign assets and UK banks run large dollar books, so a basis widening would affect both legs. The futures rolls show none. The left-side risk is already captured in Factor 3, so this factor stays Neutral.

tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.12 sits just above the +0.10 Bullish threshold. It rests on depth in two factors, not breadth. Policy & Rates (+0.149) and Inflation & Growth (+0.097) together contribute +0.246, against three Bearish factors (risk appetite, external balance, event risk) totalling -0.123. Five factors are Neutral. The call says carry and UK data momentum outweigh tail risks over four weeks, but by a margin a single factor change could erase. +0.1238 is at or above +0.10, so the net stance is Bullish; conviction is 2, at the low end of directional calls.
tactical.rationale: At tactical weights, Policy & Rates (0.27) and Inflation & Growth (0.18) dominate, and both favour the pound. The 375bp differential widens to 400bp on 5 November with no SNB meeting until 10 December, and the UK data calendar is more likely to beat expectations than the single Swiss CPI print on 3 November. The weighted score is +0.12, so the verdict is mechanically Bullish, but only just. Against it are a haven-versus-carry risk factor, the UK's energy-driven external drag, and an event set skewed towards a weaker pound and stronger franc: the post-midterm Iran window (30% escalation against 10% for a deal in the base view) and live French spread stress. The two currency views interact constructively for the pair tactically. The pound's own policy factor is Neutral because the hike is priced, but against the franc the pound holds its best carry-to-vol ratio (about 0.7 on an estimated 3-month vol of 5.4%), while the franc view is Bearish on rates because every peer is tightening around a 0% SNB. Positioning adds two-sided squeeze risk: a stretched legacy sterling short that a hawkish BoE could cover, and a record leveraged franc short that a haven shock could cover. What is priced is the November hike and about 100bp over a year. The edge is carry building up in a quiet SNB window, not the decision itself. The path of least resistance is a slow upward drift driven by carry, punctuated by event risk. The key dates are Swiss CPI and the US midterms on 3 November, the BoE Report on 5 November, UK Q3 GDP on 12 November, UK labour data on 17 November and UK October CPI in the third week of November. Conviction is held at 2 because the score clears the threshold by only 0.02, the bullish case is concentrated in two factors, and the bearish tails are sudden enough to erase weeks of carry in a session. A post-midterm US strike on Iran, or an OAT-Bund spread above 170bp, would turn the risk factor decisive and the verdict Neutral or Bearish.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Tactically sterling ranks 5th of 11 and the franc 6th in their respective currency views, so the pair is a mild long between two mid-table currencies. Among pound longs, GBP/CHF offers the best carry-to-vol of any pound cross. It ranks second behind short EUR/GBP, which removes the haven tail, and ahead of GBP/JPY, which carries a December BoJ hike risk. Among franc shorts, it ranks behind CHF/NOK, which combines better carry with oil terms of trade, and ahead of USD/CHF, where the franc view expects US rate momentum to peak.

decrease_conditions: Decrease to 1 if either: a daily close below 1.0960 (failure of the October rising-lows structure); or the OAT-Bund spread rises above 165bp.

Turn Neutral/Bearish if either: a US strike on Iran, a VIX close above 25, or an OAT-Bund spread above 170bp; or a weekly close below 1.0931. Current level 2 holds while spot trades between 1.0960 and 1.1120 and the event week is unresolved.

risk_reward.downside_case_loss: -152 pips (-1.37%) on spot; -114 pips including carry

risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: In spot terms the distribution is almost symmetric. Carry is what makes the long positive in expectation, and the downside arrives faster than the upside, as 1 October showed.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.28 is clearly Bearish, with five Bearish factors, five Neutral and none Bullish. External Balance (-0.099), Guidance (-0.066), Inflation & Growth (-0.052) and Fiscal (-0.038) carry it, and the heaviest factor, Policy & Rates, is Neutral. Breadth is doing much of the work: each Bearish factor is held at 52-62 confidence, so the score reflects many modest structural headwinds pointing the same way rather than one decisive driver. -0.2815 is at or below -0.10, so the net stance is Bearish; on the currency dossiers' scale this would be the conviction-3 band, but conviction is held at 2, chiefly because the forward already discounts much of the expected decline.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the heaviest factor, Policy & Rates (0.27), is Neutral. The pound keeps a large absolute carry advantage, but the expected change in the differential relative to pricing is negative from both central banks. So the -0.28 Bearish score comes from the structural factors: External Balance (0.16), Guidance (0.12), Inflation & Growth (0.10) and Fiscal (0.07). Here the two currency views reinforce each other strongly. The base view is Bearish on the pound strategically (-0.40), citing a 2.5%-of-GDP deficit absorbing a record winter gas forward and a BoE that delivers about 50bp less than the curve prices. The franc view is mildly Bullish on the franc (+0.13), citing a 9.2%-of-GDP surplus at the cheapest real exchange rate since at least January 2024, AAA fiscal quality and a 2027 SNB hike option the curve does not price. The pair-specific overlays add to this: the bilateral goods deficit, a commodity mix in which UK gas and gold both work against the pair, and a haven-versus-carry structure that compounds energy shocks. What is priced matters most here. The futures roll already discounts GBP/CHF falling by about 4.5% a year, roughly 2.2% over six months. Our edge is in the direction of spot and in the tails, not necessarily in beating the forward. The path of least resistance is a carry-cushioned grind lower as the winter energy bill, the SNB's December forecast and the BoE's February Report reprice the differential. The key dates are the SNB assessment and conditional forecast on 10 December, the BoE decision on 17 December and the BoE Report on 4 February 2027, whose date is provisional. Conviction is 2 rather than 3 for three reasons. The Bearish factors each sit at modest confidence. The forward already prices much of the expected decline, so a short pays carry that our base case only partly beats. And the published bank view, led by UBS, still favours the pair on carry. A BoE that validates three hikes by spring, or a Hormuz settlement that pulls UK gas forwards sharply lower, would remove the external and policy legs of the case.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically sterling ranks 8th of 11 and the franc 4th in their respective currency views, which makes GBP/CHF one of the wider bearish gaps among the pound's crosses. Among pound shorts it ranks behind GBP/NOK, where carry and terms of trade both favour the krone, and roughly level with GBP/CAD. It ranks ahead of GBP/USD, where the Fed is also hiking. Among franc longs it ranks behind CHF/JPY shorts (the yen as the preferred haven) and level with EUR/CHF shorts. The franc's advantage over the pound is the strongest of its deficit-currency comparisons alongside AUD/CHF.

conditions: The BoE stops at 4.25%, the 4 February 2027 Report signals that level is sufficient, and the 2027 strip reprices 40-60bp lower.
The SNB's 10 December forecast raises 2027 inflation to 0.9-1.0% and the Swiss 2-year yield rises above 0.30%.
UK gas forwards stay above 200p/therm through the winter and the Q4 2026 UK current account deficit widens above 3% of GDP.
base_case.path: -282 pips (-2.55%) from spot. That leaves the pair just above the four-touch 1.0723-1.0735 zone and the 200-day average, and 34 pips below the six-month forward of 1.0794. The pair holds 1.0985-1.1150 through mid-December, then breaks below 1.0960 and 1.0931 in January on the Ofgem cap, UK CPI and Q4 trade data, and the 4 February Report carries it through 1.0850-1.0890 towards 1.0760.

conditions: The BoE hikes three times to 4.50% by May 2027.
A US-Iran settlement reopens Hormuz and UK gas forwards fall below 150p/therm.
The SNB forecast is unchanged at 0.8% for 2027 and Swiss CPI prints 0.8% or less.
A winter Gulf escalation takes Brent above $140 and triggers a haven rush into the franc.
Spring fiscal slippage takes the UK 30-year gilt back above 6.10%.
The SNB hikes in March 2027 or signals one in December.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic decline should start only after the tactical carry window has played out. From November to mid-December the pair holds a 1.0985-1.1150 range with the tactical upside bias, accruing carry for longs and costing shorts about 41 pips a month. The mid-December inflection follows: the SNB's 10 December forecast and the BoE's 17 December vote split are the first tests, and a firmer Swiss path and fewer than three BoE hawks would start the turn. In January the Ofgem cap, December UK CPI and the first Q4 trade data should break the pair below 1.0960 and then the 1.0931 top of the two-touch zone, with realised volatility rising towards 6%. From February to April the provisional 4 February Report should carry the move through 1.0850-1.0890 towards 1.0760, above the four-touch 1.0723-1.0735 zone. Rallies should be capped inside the ten-touch 1.10955-1.11969 band. The shape is a carry-cushioned grind lower with one or two sharp haven-driven legs, not a steady trend. By late April the 200-week average, declining to about 1.0984, would sit more than 200 pips above spot in the base case.

increase_conditions: Increase to 3 if either: the SNB's 10 December forecast shows 2027 inflation at 1.0% or more, followed by a weekly close below 1.0931; or the Q4 2026 UK current account deficit comes in above 3% of GDP with UK gas forwards above 220p/therm.

Increase to 4 if both: a weekly close below 1.0723 (the four-touch zone and the 200-day average), and the 2027 BoE strip prices a terminal of 4.25% or less while the Swiss 2-year yield rises above 0.30%.
decrease_conditions: Decrease to 1 if either: a weekly close above 1.1197 (the top of the ten-touch band) confirmed by a second week; or the BoE signals a February hike while the SNB's December forecast is unchanged at 0.8%.

Turn Neutral if either: a Hormuz settlement holds for four weeks with UK gas forwards below 150p/therm; or SNB domestic sight deposits rise more than CHF 10bn in four weeks, signalling active franc selling. Current level 2 holds while the 2027 BoE strip prices 75-100bp, the SNB is priced on hold into mid-2027, and spot trades between 1.0931 and 1.1197.

risk_reward.base_case_payoff: +282 pips (+2.55%) for a short from 1.10417 to 1.0760
risk_reward.downside_case_loss: -258 pips (-2.34%) in the upside scenario (1.1300); the downside scenario (1.0620) pays +422 pips (+3.82%)
risk_reward.risk_reward_ratio: 1.09:1 (base-case reward to upside-scenario loss, on spot)
risk_reward.expected_value: Spot: 0.50 x 282 + 0.25 x 422 - 0.25 x 258 = 141 + 105.5 - 64.5 = +182 pips (+1.65%). A six-month forward sold at 1.0794 at today's spot: base +34, upside-scenario loss -506, downside-scenario gain +174, expected value 0.50 x 34 + 0.25 x 174 - 0.25 x 506 = -66 pips (probability-weighted spot of about 1.0860 sits 66 pips above the forward). The same forward sold after a rally to 1.1125 spot (forward about 1.0876): +116, -424, +256, expected value +16 pips.
risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: In spot terms the distribution favours the bearish view. After carry it does not, unless entry is disciplined (selling into the ten-touch band) or the downside tail carries more than 25% probability.

consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast: No bank-survey median for GBP/CHF was found. Published bank research is constructive. UBS says it remains positive on the pound against the franc, expects the BoE to start a short hiking cycle with a further hike in Q1 2027, calls GBP/CHF one of the more attractive G10 total-return trades, and expects the case to become more balanced once markets anticipate SNB tightening. A numeric UBS path exists: GBP/CHF at 1.12 in December 2026, declining to 1.09 by March 2027 and 1.08 by June and September 2027, framed as carry driving the pair unless UK fiscal concerns develop into broader confidence issues. Rabobank expects the franc to stay soft while the SNB holds at zero.
consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: UBS research reported by Investing.com (late October 2026); Rabobank commentary reported by Pound Sterling Live (October 2026). Model-generated forecast pages were excluded because they are not bank research.
consensus_divergence.our_tactical_view: Bullish at conviction 2 (+0.12): carry and UK data momentum outweigh tail risks over four weeks. Broadly in line with the bank view.
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bearish at conviction 2 (-0.28): the UK external deficit, a BoE delivering less than priced, a firmer SNB path and UK fiscal fragility point to a weaker pound against the franc over one to six months.
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: In line with the constructive bank view tactically; below it strategically (same direction as the UBS path, which also turns lower into 2027).
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Directional rather than numeric: no consensus target exists to measure the gap against. Against the UBS path (roughly 1.09 in March moving to 1.08 in June), our 30 April 2027 base case of 1.0760 is about 140 pips lower, in the same direction; the gap is one of magnitude and timing, not direction.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: The bank view weights the level of carry: a 375-400bp gap and the BoE's turn make the pair a total-return trade. We weight the change in the differential against pricing, and the structural balance underneath it. The curve prices about 100bp of BoE tightening that the Committee's own hawks doubt, while the SNB's December forecast and its step back from intervention point the other way. UBS itself expects the case to become more balanced once SNB tightening is anticipated, and the franc view puts that inside the horizon. We also give more weight to the external gap of about 11.7 percentage points of GDP, the UK winter gas bill that reaches the data only from December, and a haven-versus-carry structure that compounds energy shocks.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A strategic decline in spot that beats the roughly 2.2% six-month forward discount pays a forward seller. Downside optionality pays more in a Gulf escalation or a French sovereign episode, when the decline is fastest.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the bank view is right, carry keeps building at about 4.5% a year and a short loses both carry and spot. The trigger would be a BoE that validates three hikes by spring with energy relief, or a covering of sterling shorts after a hawkish Report.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge because the weights shift from fast to slow factors. Tactically, Policy & Rates and Inflation & Growth carry 0.45 of the weight. Both favour the pound: a BoE hike in a window with no SNB meeting, and UK releases likely to beat expectations. Strategically, the policy factor turns Neutral as the repricing of the 2027 strip offsets the carry level, and the weight moves to External Balance, Guidance and Fiscal, all Bearish. UK data that look hawkish in November turn into a stagflation mix by early 2027.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Mid-December to early February. The SNB's 10 December conditional forecast is the first test of a firmer Swiss path. The BoE's 17 December decision, which has no Report, shows whether a February hike has support. The 4 February 2027 Monetary Policy Report, a provisional date, is where the base view expects the Committee to signal that 4.25% is enough. The UK January energy cap and the Q4 trade data arrive in the same window.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Express the tactical view as carry with tight risk limits through the November event cluster. Treat any strength after the 5 November decision as the place to start building strategic downside, preferably through optionality so the carry drag is not paid outright. Tactical longs enter on dips to 1.0990-1.1005, with a stop below 1.0925 and profits taken at 1.1110-1.1190. Strategic downside is built on rallies into 1.1100-1.1150, invalidated on a weekly close above 1.1200. The two plans overlap by design: the zone where tactical profits are taken is the zone where strategic shorts are built.

forward_vs_spot.edge_3m: +32 pips pound-favourable: expected spot of 1.0950 is already below today's spot but still above the 1.0918 forward, so a forward seller would still be under water. (One-month edge: expected 1.1110 vs forward 1.1001, +109 pips pound-favourable.)

catalysts.rationale: September CPI was 1.0% with core at 0.5%. A print of 1.2% or more would revive December SNB hike pricing from about 6bp and lower the pair by narrowing the expected differential. A print of 0.8% or less would confirm the hold and support carry, lifting the pair.

catalysts.event: US midterm elections, after which the White House has said strikes on Iran become possible
catalysts.rationale: Escalation hits GBP/CHF through both legs at once: higher UK gas and oil costs weigh on an energy importer with a deficit, and a haven bid lifts the franc. The base view puts escalation within four weeks at 30% and a Hormuz framework at 10%, so the probabilities lean against the pair.

catalysts.event: Bank of England decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: A 25bp hike to 4.00% is about 95% priced and widens the differential to 400bp, so the vote split and the conditioned projections decide the reaction. A 7-2 or 8-1 hike with inflation near target at three years would be a dovish hike that trims 2027 pricing. A 9-0 vote with guidance for more would squeeze sterling shorts and lift the pair.

Reserves were CHF 770.48bn in September. A rise beyond valuation effects would be the first sign the SNB is leaning against franc strength again despite dropping its increased willingness to intervene. That would cap franc gains and is mildly supportive for the pair.

catalysts.event: UK Q3 GDP preliminary estimate, September monthly GDP and trade
catalysts.rationale: BoE staff estimated Q3 at 0.4% q/q, while the three months to August grew 0.7%. A print of 0.5% or more would support February hike odds and the pound's carry against a franc with no domestic catalyst until December. The trade figures give an early read on the energy bill.

catalysts.event: UK labour market release (three months to September)
catalysts.rationale: Unemployment fell to 4.7% with regular pay at 3.7%. A rebound towards 5.0% would undercut the BoE hiking path and the pair's rate support. Pay growth above 3.8% would sustain the divergence against Swiss wage growth of 0.4%.

catalysts.event: Ofgem announcement of the January 2027 household energy price cap (exact date not confirmed; week 4 of November)
catalysts.rationale: The cap passes the record Q1 2027 gas forward, near 238p/therm, to UK households from January. That lifts the Q1 CPI peak for the wrong reasons and squeezes real incomes, reinforcing the stagflation reading behind strategic Factor 2. Switzerland has no equivalent energy-bill shock, so the effect is one-sided for the pair.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal votes (AHV VAT financing, married-couple taxation, war-material act, fireworks)
catalysts.rationale: None of the four proposals changes the Swiss macro picture. Approving VAT funding for the AHV pension system is a small fiscal-sustainability positive that reinforces the AAA contrast with the UK, but it is not a market event for the cross.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: A hike to 4.00-4.25% strengthens the dollar against both legs about equally, so the direct effect on the cross is small. A Fed that also signals the end of its cycle would move the dollar towards the middle of the smile, where franc-funded carry loses some of its tailwind.

catalysts.event: SNB quarterly monetary policy assessment with new conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The franc view expects the forecast to raise 2027 inflation to 0.9-1.0% at a 0% rate. Any hint of a 2027 hike would narrow the expected differential and lower the pair. A hold with an unchanged forecast would extend the carry regime. This is the most important franc catalyst of the horizon.

catalysts.event: Bank of England decision (no Monetary Policy Report)
catalysts.rationale: A hold is likely after November. The vote split will show whether a February hike has support. Fewer than three votes for a hike would support the strategic view that the BoE stops early, while a hawkish split would lift the pair. It comes a week after the SNB, so the ordering matters.

A BoJ hike to 1.50% matters for this cross through the funding channel. A hike makes the yen more expensive to borrow, and franc-funded carry has been the beneficiary: market commentary describes the start of a rotation to the Swiss franc as the funder of choice, which would weigh on the franc and support the pair. If the hike instead triggers a yen-led carry unwind, the franc's haven role dominates and the pair falls.

catalysts.event: Bank of England decision with Monetary Policy Report (provisional date)
catalysts.rationale: The base view expects the Committee to signal that about 4.25% is enough, repricing the 2027 strip lower by 40-60bp and narrowing the pound's expected advantage over the franc. This is the main strategic inflection point. The date is provisional and not yet confirmed by the Bank.

invalidators.condition: GBP/CHF posts a weekly close above 1.1200, the top of the ten-touch 1.10955-1.11969 band, confirmed by a second week
invalidators.mechanism: A sustained break of the best-tested supply on the chart would mean carry is beating the external and policy-repricing case. It would also open the second ten-touch band at 1.1236-1.1344 and the UBS December level of 1.12.

invalidators.condition: A US strike on Iran lifts Brent above $130, or the OAT-Bund spread closes above 170bp, inside the next four weeks
invalidators.mechanism: Either event activates both legs against the pair at once: an energy shock for the pound and a haven bid for the franc. That would overwhelm a carry accrual of about 41 pips a month, as the 1 October session showed.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Brent front-month and the French-German 10-year spread

invalidators.condition: The SNB's 10 December conditional forecast leaves 2027 inflation at 0.8% or lower while the BoE's 17 December vote shows three or more members for a February hike
invalidators.mechanism: The differential would then widen by at least as much as the futures price, removing the guidance and policy-surprise legs of the bearish case.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB conditional forecast and BoE vote split

invalidators.condition: The UK Q1 2027 gas forward falls below 150p/therm for ten sessions
invalidators.mechanism: The UK terms-of-trade shock behind the highest-confidence factor (External Balance, 62) would reverse, and the de-escalation that drives it would also drain the franc's haven premium.

invalidators.condition: GBP/CHF closes below 1.0960 on a daily basis while leveraged-fund franc shorts are covered to below 10,000 contracts
invalidators.mechanism: That combination would show a haven-led unwind of the pair's own carry trade under way, not a one-day wobble, breaking the October rising-lows structure.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: GBP/CHF daily close and the CFTC leveraged-fund CHF net

invalidators.condition: SNB domestic sight deposits rise by more than CHF 10bn over four weeks
invalidators.mechanism: Active SNB franc selling would cap the franc's gains against the pound and limit the downside the strategic view needs.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB weekly sight deposits against the CHF 435.36bn level of mid-October

signposts.indicator: GBP/CHF futures-implied carry (CME franc-sterling calendar spread)
signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: the premium holds beyond -440bp after the 5 November hike; strategic: it compresses inside -400bp by February 2027.
signposts.invalidates_if: Strategic: it widens beyond -475bp, as both central banks validate a wider gap.
signposts.bilateral_importance: It is the single market price of the pair's defining feature, the carry. It measures the expected differential directly rather than through either leg alone.

signposts.indicator: UK 2-year gilt minus Swiss 2-year Confederation yield
signposts.confirms_if: Strategic: it narrows below 430bp as the 2027 BoE strip reprices or Swiss hike pricing builds.
signposts.bilateral_importance: Both ends of the strategic policy-surprise argument show up in this one spread, which neither currency view tracks alone.

signposts.confirms_if: Strategic: it rises above 0.30% as a 2027 SNB hike is priced.
signposts.invalidates_if: Strategic: it falls below 0.05%, pricing out any 2027 move.
signposts.bilateral_importance: UBS itself expects the pair's case to become more balanced once markets anticipate SNB tightening, so this is the cleanest early read on that turn.

signposts.current_level: About 238p/therm (30 October); record close for the contract on 28 October
signposts.confirms_if: Strategic: it stays above 220p/therm through December.
signposts.invalidates_if: Strategic: it falls below 150p/therm for two weeks.
signposts.bilateral_importance: Gas is one-sided for this cross. It hits the pound's terms of trade and leaves the franc, with energy at about 3.5% of its CPI, almost untouched.

signposts.indicator: CFTC positioning: CHF leveraged funds and GBP legacy non-commercial
signposts.current_level: CHF leveraged -17,502 contracts; GBP legacy -79,400 (week to 27 October)
signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: the franc short stays above 15,000 while the sterling legacy short covers towards -60,000.
signposts.invalidates_if: Tactical: the franc leveraged short is covered below 10,000 with spot falling, the signature of a haven squeeze of the pair's carry trade.
signposts.bilateral_importance: The pair-level carry trade is visible only by combining the two legs. Each leg on its own describes a different investor.

signposts.confirms_if: Tactical: it eases below 140bp, draining the franc's haven bid.
signposts.bilateral_importance: European sovereign stress is the haven channel most specific to the franc. It reaches GBP/CHF whenever franc gains against the euro outpace the pound's.

signposts.current_level: CHF 435.36bn domestic, CHF 457.01bn total (week to 16 October)
signposts.confirms_if: Strategic: weekly changes stay within +/-CHF 5bn, confirming no intervention against franc strength.
signposts.invalidates_if: Strategic: there is a four-week rise above CHF 10bn.
signposts.bilateral_importance: Intervention is the only mechanism that can cap the franc's strategic gains against the pound, so it bounds the downside scenario.

assumptions: Price data: the series is daily closing prices for 130 weekday sessions from 2026-05-04 to 2026-10-30. Spot is 1.10417 at the 30 October 2026 close.

The valuation date, 1 November 2026, falls two calendar days later over a weekend, so no trading session is missing between spot and valuation. Every level, distance and pip figure is anchored to that close.

Moving averages, 200-week figures and support and resistance zones are computed over the full stored history: 4,921 weekday sessions from 2007-12-21 to 2026-10-30 (plus 1,011 weekly and 502 monthly bars). Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes; realised volatility is annualised on 252 trading days; ATR(14) is 48 pips.

The 52-week range is quoted on both an intraday basis (1.02857-1.11079, spot at the 92nd percentile) and a closing basis (1.03555-1.10859, spot at the 94th percentile). Narrative prose and this JSON use the closing basis.

Support and resistance zones are clustered weekly and monthly swing closes with stated touch counts. Distances are quoted to zone midpoints, with zone edges stated where they matter for execution. The symmetrical-triangle description combines daily highs and lows with dealer commentary; trendline levels are approximate.

The factor stances rest on fundamentals only. The pair's own trading, trend and levels enter only Factor 9 and the trade plans, scenarios, invalidators and signposts. Weight adjustments are +0.03 on Factor 1, +0.02 on Factor 3 and -0.05 on Factor 10, on both horizons; weights sum to 1.00.

Policy rates are Bank Rate 3.75% (as of 26 October) and the SNB at 0% (as of 27 October), a 375bp differential. The 10-year yields in the monthly series are September averages (UK 5.24%, Switzerland 0.59%, a 465bp gap), not live levels; live comparisons use 30 October closes: gilts 5.29% and Swiss 0.47%, a 482bp gap.

Futures-implied carry of 448.7bp is the annualised December 2026 to March 2027 calendar spread between listed CME franc and sterling futures, observed 29 October. It combines the rate differential and any cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated. Forward points apply that rate to spot on an actual/365 basis. The annualised_carry_bps and carry_to_vol_ratio fields use the 375bp policy carry (0.69); the futures-implied figures are 448.7bp and about 0.83.

Pair implied volatility is an estimate, not a quote, because no GBP/CHF option is listed. It is built from the two dollar legs with a realised correlation of 0.636, observed 29 October at tenors of 35.7, 98.7 and 189.6 days. The method has run 9-18% low against direct quotes, so carry-to-vol ratios are overstated to that extent. Cross skew is inferred from the GBP/USD and USD/CHF risk reversals of 28 October.

Bilateral goods trade is 2024 IMF Direction of Trade data. Mirror figures disagree (Swiss-reported exports to the UK $22.6bn against UK-reported imports from Switzerland $12.8bn), most plausibly because of gold routing, so the UK-reported net balance of -$3.5bn is used.

CFTC percentiles cover only the 25 weekly reports since 12 May 2026, not a multi-year history; no explicit percentile was published for the sterling position (base_cftc_percentile null) and the franc leveraged short is the most short of the 25 weeks (percentile 0 on that window). The implied-vol percentile was not computed (iv_percentile null).
BoE and SNB market pricing comes from bank and press summaries; no SONIA or SARON OIS strip was available.
Scenario probabilities are fixed at 50/25/25. Carry figures in the risk/reward use the futures-implied rate. Position sizes assume 0.5% of capital at risk per trade at conviction 2.
The UK October CPI and Ofgem cap dates were not confirmed and are shown by week; the Ofgem catalyst date 2026-11-25 is a placeholder within week 4 of November.
